**filed: 2026-05-24**

The two existing-file evidence anchors now live at `release/references/pipeline/stage-05-solutioning.md` and `core/standards/principal-standard-checklist.md`._

### Category
Enhancement

### Description

Two paired Stage 5 gaps: (a) No formal "design-idea exploration → alternative elimination" tooling — current trade-off matrix exists but doesn't enforce mind-map-style alternative generation followed by narrowing; (b) No DOMAIN-SPECIFIC best-practices reference library — Principal Standard checklist is cross-domain but doesn't tailor to software (scalability/maintainability/simplicity-first), hardware (reliability), governance (compliance), etc. Both limit design rigor at Stage 5.

## Description

The pattern is UNANIMOUS systemic — every phase's load-bearing quality attribute lacks canonical observability instrumentation at the cross-release telemetry layer.

9.title: [Process]: Phase 3 PII concentration threshold over-triggers on multi-match tickets — v18.04+ scanner amendment
9.body:
**filed: 2026-05-28**

### Priority

P3 — Quality improvement; not blocking v18.03b; v18.04+ scanner amendment

### Category

Process

### Description

Phase 3 PII concentration threshold (per `pmo-platform/reference/standards/public-flip-readiness-gate-framework.md § 3.1` + AUTOMATION_PLAN.md Section 14 implemented in `scan-v2-issues-for-pii.py` per #2933 Pass 2) computes:

```
concentration = total_matches / scanned_issues
```

This counts ALL PII regex matches across ALL issues, NOT unique flagged tickets. **Defect scenario:** 5 tickets × 5 matches each = 25 matches / 100-ticket scan = 25% trip — even though only 5% of tickets carry PII.

The threshold may over-trigger on substrates that are only-marginally-non-clean — operator hits a HALT-before-Pass-2 condition on a single ticket with many matches, when the substrate is otherwise within accepted tolerance.

### Evidence

[SOURCE: 2026-05-27 v18.03b Cycle 4 Adversarial #2969 FM-2 Minor] Adversarial review of #2941 Stage 5 (Phase 3 design) surfaced the residual. Spec author selected current behavior (Option A) at D-PIIGateSemantics Q1 because Option B "would require a Tier 1 [ADJUST] back to the scanner" — but the over-trigger pattern was not converted into a "what if this fires falsely" failure mode at Stage 5 time.

[INFERRED] Operator has `--skip-pii-gate` override flag (per #2925 Pass 2 Section 9) available if Phase 3 PII gate trips falsely during v18.03b execution. So this is NOT blocking v18.03b — operator can override and route per AUTOMATION_PLAN.md Section 14 (c-i) Fix-forward.

[CONTEXT: `public-flip-readiness-gate-framework.md § 3.1`] Authority framework's primitive 3 (DC1 PII) is designed for git-history-grep + manual disposition; concentration math is workspace adaptation in v18.03b release-engineering surface.

### Affected Files

- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/scan-v2-issues-for-pii.py` (lines around concentration computation; specific lines depend on v18.03b Engineering Commit 0 implementation per #2933 Pass 2)
- Possibly `pmo-platform/reference/standards/public-flip-readiness-gate-framework.md` if the upstream framework spec needs updating to clarify the concentration semantic

### Documentation Impact

- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/scan-v2-issues-for-pii.py` | update | swap concentration numerator from `total_matches` to `unique_flagged_issues`
- v18.04+ release plan | update | reference this Issue as in-scope hardening item

### Proposed Change

**OUTCOME:** Phase 3 PII concentration threshold computes:

```
concentration = unique_flagged_issues / scanned_issues
```

Where `unique_flagged_issues` = count of distinct v2 issue numbers in `pii-flag-queue.md` (one issue per concentration count regardless of how many regex matches that issue carries).

**Implementation:** In `scan-v2-issues-for-pii.py`, replace the per-match counter with a per-issue set; emit concentration as `len(unique_flagged_set) / total_scanned`. Preserves current `--output-format` semantics; only changes the gate-decision math.

**Test fixtures:**
- Positive case: 1 ticket × 5 matches → concentration = 1/100 = 1% (gate PASS) vs. current behavior 5/100 = 5% (still PASS but mis-reported)
- Critical case: 5 tickets × 5 matches each → concentration = 5/100 = 5% (gate PASS) vs. current behavior 25/100 = 25% (gate TRIP — false positive)
- Boundary case: 25 tickets × 1 match each → concentration = 25/100 = 25% (gate TRIP — correct behavior; semantic unchanged)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scan-v2-issues-for-pii.py` concentration computation uses `unique_flagged_issues / scanned_issues` numerator
- [ ] Test fixtures cover positive / critical / boundary cases above
- [ ] `--output-format json` schema unchanged (per CD-1 cross-spoke contract preserved)
- [ ] `--output-format markdown` `pii-flag-queue.md` head matrix unchanged (per [ADJUST-5] convention preserved)
- [ ] Concentration value emitted in stderr log shows BOTH `unique` and `total_matches` counts for operator transparency

### Dependencies

- After v18.03b (this carry-forward — release closes before this fires)
- Composes with v18.04+ scanner amendments per future Stage 4 D-decisions

10.title: [Structure]: Repo platform adapter parameterization — GitHub abstraction enabling GitLab / Bitbucket / Azure DevOps Repos / self-hosted Git
10.body:
**filed: 2026-05-27**

### Priority

P3 - Medium

### Category

Structure

### Description

Operator vision (2026-05-27): "For the ticketing side, it is also their ticketing in their repo locations. So understanding where their repos are stored, how they manage their tickets today, and ensuring that the harness is set up and able to accept the majority."

Today pmo-platform is GitHub-CLI-coupled throughout: `gh` invocations are pervasive in `deploy.sh`, stage docs, skills, pipeline references. The repo-platform abstraction is a load-bearing implicit assumption with zero parameterization seam.

This ticket establishes repo-platform parameterization: GitHub abstracted as one of N supported repo platforms (GitLab / Bitbucket / Azure DevOps Repos / Codeberg / Gitea / self-hosted Git) with a configured platform choice.

### Evidence

- [SOURCE: operator direction 2026-05-27] — "understanding where their repos are stored ... harness is set up and able to accept the majority."
- [SOURCE: `deploy.sh` + every stage doc] — `gh` CLI invocations are pervasive; no abstraction layer exists.
- [SOURCE: `[internal note]` § 5 G4] — Gap identified: zero open tickets for non-GitHub repo platforms.
- [CONTEXT: `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`] — git workflow is platform-agnostic; only the issue/PR side is GitHub-specific.

### Affected Files

[ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] TBD — Stage 5 will determine. Likely candidates:

- `pmo-platform-v2/core/reference/repo-platforms-v1.md` (create — enumerate supported platforms)
- `deploy.sh` (audit — every `gh` invocation; abstract via per-platform command shim)
- `pmo-platform-v2/release/skills/*/SKILL.md` (audit — release skills that hardcode `gh`)
- `pmo-platform-v2/core/config/repo-platform.yaml.template` (create — operator declares platform at install time)

### Documentation Impact

- `pmo-platform-v2/core/reference/repo-platforms-v1.md` | create | enumerate supported platforms with command-shim docs
- `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md` | update | declare platform-agnostic-vs-platform-specific sections

**filed: 2026-05-27**

### Description

Operator vision (2026-05-27): "I want anybody to be able to use this harness on a tool that supports this kind of work. So Claude code, code, um, maybe GPT or Copilot, those types of things. And the harness needs to be able to support those in the config process."

- [CONTEXT: [#364](https://github.com/cody-hutson/pmo-platform/issues/364)] — Skills-distribution / multi-tenant deployment research includes multi-tenant deployment scope; multi-AI-tool was elevated as Stage 5 design input via comment 2026-05-27 but is not yet a tracked deliverable.

15.title: [Skill Update]: ADR-creation helper skill — scaffold ADR-NNN.md files at decision moments
15.body:
**filed: 2026-05-27**

### Priority

P4 - Low

### Category

Skill Update

### Description

pmo-platform has ADR-001 through ADR-005 manually authored at `pmo-platform/governance/adr/`. The format is consistent, but creating one is friction — the operator must remember the structure, allocate the next number, write the canonical sections. Friction depresses ADR authoring-rate, so decisions get lost to commit messages and Slack threads instead.

An ADR-creation helper skill auto-detects decision moments (operator says "let's record this", chooses between significant alternatives), scaffolds `ADR-NNN.md` with the canonical structure (Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered / Consequences / Status), allocates the next sequential number, and writes the file ready for operator editing.

### Evidence

- [CONTEXT: `pmo-platform/governance/adr/ADR-001..005`] — manual authoring works but friction is real; ADRs are written rarely (5 in the platform's history despite many qualifying decisions).
- [CONTEXT: `pmo-platform/reference/explanation/decision-discipline.md`] — framework defines the decision-class surface; no current friction-reducer exists for the framework's primary artifact.

### Affected Files

- `pmo-platform/skills/adr-helper/SKILL.md` (create — new skill)
- `pmo-platform/skills/adr-helper/references/` (create — skill references)
- `deploy.sh` `SKILL_LIST` (edit — register new skill)

[ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] TBD — additional reference docs identified in Planning

### Documentation Impact

- `pmo-platform/skills/adr-helper/SKILL.md` | create | new skill
- `pmo-platform/skills/adr-helper/references/*.md` | create | skill references
- `pmo-platform/reference/explanation/decision-discipline.md` | link | cite ADR-helper as the friction-reducer for ADR authoring
- `pmo-platform/governance/OPERATIONS.md` | update | register new skill
- `.claude/rules/skill-deployment.md` | update | add to SKILL_LIST documented in deploy steps

### Proposed Change

The outcome: a new pmo-platform skill recognizes decision moments and offers ADR scaffolding. Skill writes `ADR-NNN.md` to `pmo-platform/governance/adr/` (or pmo-platform-v2 equivalent post-restructure) with canonical structure. Skill auto-allocates the next sequential ADR number. Composes with `decision-discipline.md` — this skill is the friction-reducer for the framework's primary artifact.

NOT IN SCOPE (defer to Stage 5):

- Auto-detection mechanism (LLM-graded vs explicit-trigger-only)
- Whether skill writes draft content or only scaffolds structure
- ADR-renumbering on supersession (handled today by `Status: superseded by ADR-NNN`)

[ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] mechanism TBD at Stage 5

### Dependencies

None at intake. Composes with `decision-discipline.md` framework.

### Risks & Cross-Cutting Impact

- [INFERRED] Auto-detection may produce false positives ("offered ADR scaffolding when operator didn't want one"). Mitigation: scaffolding offer is non-blocking; operator declines without friction.
- [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] Post-restructure (v18.02 module-restructure), the ADR home path may change to `pmo-platform-v2/governance/adr/` or per-module ADR locations per P2-T9. Skill must read the canonical ADR home location dynamically, not hardcode.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pmo-platform/skills/adr-helper/SKILL.md` exists with frontmatter conforming to `canonical-skill-structure.md` (method: `deploy.sh --check` Check 6 passes for the new skill)
- [ ] Skill produces a valid `ADR-NNN.md` file at the canonical ADR home when invoked (method: trigger via test prompt; verify file exists with canonical sections)
- [ ] Auto-allocated ADR number is one higher than the current maximum existing ADR (method: list `pmo-platform/governance/adr/ADR-*.md`, sort, take tail; generated filename matches the next sequential number)
- [ ] Skill registered in `deploy.sh` SKILL_LIST + `OPERATIONS.md` skill catalog (method: `deploy.sh --check` Check 5 passes)

### Notes

Origin: an external harness review 2026-05-27 (`[internal note]` § 9c ET-8).

Composes with v18.02 P2-T9 (ADR relocation per per-module placement) — if ADR home changes post-restructure, this skill must read the canonical location dynamically.

No suggested bundle target at intake — Triage decides.

### Description

18.title: [Protocol]: Eliminate bypass-mode-readiness.md cascade-conflict class via per-hook file split (D1/D2/D3 options)
18.body:
**filed: 2026-05-27**

### Priority

P2 — Structural cascade-conflict prevention; target v18.02 (BEFORE Phase 2 module restructure adds new hooks)

### Category

Process / Protocol — governance-doc architecture refactor; eliminate parallel-PR cascade-conflict class

### Description

**Observed pattern (N=2 within v18.01-monolith-cleanup release, 2026-05-27):**

| Cascade event | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| PR #2839 (#1059 fs-boundary hook) BLOCKED at Stage 12 Phase B1 | PR #2830 (#1080 shell-injection hook) merged first; both append to `bypass-mode-readiness.md` rule registry + mirror | Fix-forward chip rebase (PR HEAD `8106267`) — UNION conflict resolution |
| PR #2842 (#2536 subagent-security-posture) BLOCKED at Stage 12 Phase B1 RESUME | PR #2839 fs-boundary hook restructured `## The N Hooks` heading 5→6→7 + extended Allowlist/Warn-Mode/Recovery sections; #2842's expected base diverges | Fix-forward chip rebase (in progress at filing time) |

**Root cause:** `bypass-mode-readiness.md` (+ mirror at `core/rules/bypass-mode-readiness.md`) is a monolithic file with shared structure (rule registry, allowlist table, warn-mode list, "## The N Hooks" heading, recovery procedures). EVERY hook PR modifies multiple sections of the SAME file. Parallel PRs at scaffolding time → cascade at merge time. Mirror pair doubles the surface.

**Forward risk:** v18.02+ Phase 2 module restructure + downstream security work will continue adding hooks → same cascade keeps firing → ongoing rebase tax per release.

### Evidence

[SOURCE: Stage 12 Execute escalation 2026-05-27] `gh api repos/cody-hutson/pmo-platform/issues/comments/4554718168` — first cascade event detail.

[SOURCE: Stage 12 Resume escalation 2026-05-27] `gh api repos/cody-hutson/pmo-platform/issues/comments/4555175830` — second cascade event detail; identifies recurring class.

[SOURCE: Operator directive 2026-05-27 v18.01 hub session] "I want to ensure we don't compound issues, we use simplicity first mindset, and focus on high quality/durable/scalable fixes following best practice."

[INFERRED] Current pattern violates change-locality DRY: shared-file conflicts proportional to N×concurrent-PRs touching the file.

### Proposed Change — 3 structural options (operator picks at v18.02 triage)

**(D1) Per-hook file split:**
- Split `bypass-mode-readiness.md` into per-hook files: `bypass-mode-readiness/block-destructive.md`, `bypass-mode-readiness/block-egress.md`, etc.
- Top-level `bypass-mode-readiness.md` becomes a thin index (heading + auto-generated TOC + cross-references)
- Adding a hook = creating a new file (no shared-file conflicts)
- Mirror pair maintained per-file
- Trade-off: more files to navigate; cross-references between hooks need explicit handling

**(D2) Generated index pattern:**
- Per-hook source files at `core/standards/hooks/<hook-name>.md`
- `bypass-mode-readiness.md` auto-generated at deploy time from per-hook sources via `deploy.sh` Check N
- Adding a hook = creating source file + regenerating
- Mirror pair stays as generated artifacts
- Trade-off: generation step adds tooling; debugging requires understanding source vs generated

**(D3) Section-scoped append discipline:**
- Keep monolithic file but enforce strict "append-only at marked anchors" via lint check (new `deploy.sh` Check N)
- Anchors: `<!-- BEGIN_HOOK_REGISTRY -->`, `<!-- END_HOOK_REGISTRY -->`, etc.
- Each PR appends new content at the anchor; never modifies existing rows
- Trade-off: lower lift but doesn't fully eliminate cascade (PRs still touch same file; just same anchor row); preserves some cascade risk

**Recommended:** (D1) per-hook file split — most fully eliminates the cascade class; aligns with the self-containment discipline (#1806) for in-repo cross-references.

### Affected Files (if D1 chosen)

- `.claude/rules/bypass-mode-readiness.md` → split into directory + thin index
- `core/rules/bypass-mode-readiness.md` → mirror restructure
- `deploy.sh` Check 9 (mirror-pair sync) — update to handle directory vs single file
- All cross-references to `bypass-mode-readiness.md § <section>` need rewriting

### Documentation Impact

- `.claude/rules/bypass-mode-readiness.md` — restructure (or generate; choice per option)
- `core/rules/bypass-mode-readiness.md` — mirror
- `core/standards/canonical-skill-structure.md` — references (if any)
- All cross-references in other docs

### Dependencies

- Composes with v18.02 Phase 2 module restructure (per `~/Claude/[internal note]` § 7.3): natural alignment — file split fits the modular-monolith architecture
- Composes with #1806 self-containment discipline (in-repo cross-references)
- Composes with #1059 + #1080 + #2536 (current v18.01 hooks that landed via cascade-conflict pattern)
- Sister recurring-pattern concern: any other monolithic governance doc with similar multi-PR contribution surface (TBD per audit)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Operator-rendered choice of (D1/D2/D3) at v18.02 triage
- [ ] If D1 or D2: restructure executed; deploy.sh Check 9 updated; all cross-references rewritten
- [ ] If D3: anchored-append convention codified + lint check added
- [ ] Post-fix verification: simulate concurrent PRs each adding a new hook; verify no cascade conflict at merge time

### Notes

This is the second instance of the cascade-conflict class within v18.01. Per `decision-discipline.md § 4.1` emergence rule, N=2 same (domain, theme) within 180 days promotes to permanent pattern — but the operator's directive is to address the root cause structurally rather than just log as observation. Filed as enhancement with recommended v18.02 target.

20.title: [Protocol]: --force-with-lease unsafe under multi-chip parallel Engineering (Wave-N pattern)
20.body:
**filed: 2026-05-27**

> _Issue/sub-task numbers, commit SHAs, and version labels in this record document the v18.01 near-miss in the pre-2026-06 re-versioning scheme and are retained as historical record. File paths below are reconciled to current homes (`pmo-platform/*` → `core/` `release/`)._

### Priority

P2 — Process protocol gap with observed near-miss in v18.01 Wave 1 parallel Engineering

### Category

Process / Protocol

### Description

**Observed pattern.** v18.01 Wave 1 parallel Engineering (#305 spoke; 2026-05-27): spoke attempted `git push --force-with-lease` to remove its own commit from `release/v18.01-monolith-cleanup`. In the interval between lease-check and push, a sibling Wave 1 chip (#990 series) had committed 4 commits on top. The lease was stale, the force-push succeeded, and the spoke momentarily rewound the sibling's commits. Spoke noticed, immediately restored by re-pushing the original chain at HEAD `197c036`. Net result: release branch chain unchanged from intended state, no work lost.

**Why this matters.** Under multi-chip parallel Engineering (D-C SINGLE topology with Wave 1+ launch pattern), `--force-with-lease` is INSUFFICIENT as a safety mechanism. The lease assumes single-writer; with N concurrent chips, the lease check + push window is racy. Even a momentary rewind risks losing sibling work if the spoke does not immediately notice and recover.

**Mitigation (operator + agent guidance).** Stage 6 chip prompts under D-C SINGLE multi-chip topology MUST instruct:
1. **NEVER `git push --force` OR `--force-with-lease` to a shared release branch** when concurrent chips operate
2. **Correct path** when noticing the false-alarm "need to remove my own commit": leave the commit, create a stacked feature branch alongside (which is what #305 spoke did in the end)
3. **Recovery path** if force-push happens: immediately re-push the original chain HEAD; flag in handoff payload as a recovery action

### Evidence

[SOURCE: #305 sub-task #2760 handoff payload comment 4550961151 — recovery note section] Spoke documented the entire sequence + recovery + parallel-chip discipline lesson learned.

[SOURCE: `core/rules/git-workflow.md` § What NOT To Do] — "Never force push: `git push --force` is denied in settings.json" — but `--force-with-lease` is NOT denied (it's the safer variant). The new observation is that even `--force-with-lease` is insufficient under multi-chip parallelism.

[CONTEXT] v18.01 is the first release to use Wave-N parallel Engineering chip launches at meaningful scale under D-C SINGLE topology. Prior releases used 1-chip-at-a-time serialization, which made `--force-with-lease` safe.

[INFERRED] Under D-C OPTION-A (per-issue branches + per-issue PRs) the issue is moot — each branch has a single writer. Under D-C SINGLE with Wave-N parallelism, the new discipline is required.

### Proposed Change

1. Update `hub-spoke-bridge.md` Procedure 3 § Worktree Discipline (Stage 6 Engineering) — add explicit anti-pattern: "NEVER `--force-with-lease` to a shared release branch under multi-chip parallel-launch context"
2. Update `release/references/specs/release-personas.md` Stage 6 (Software Engineer — Implementation) anti-pattern list — same
3. Update `.claude/rules/release-process.md` § Stage 6 — codify the Wave-N parallel-Engineering safety discipline (NEVER force-push variants on shared release branch)
4. Consider adding a `block-destructive.sh` hook rule for `git push --force-with-lease` to a release branch — defense-in-depth (current rule BLOCK-DESTRUCTIVE-001 blocks `--force` / `-f` but allows `--force-with-lease`)
5. Update CHANGELOG / RELEASE_LOG learnings-triple at Stage 13 close to surface this as the v18.01 "would-change" learning

### Affected Files

- `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md` § Procedure 3 § Worktree Discipline
- `release/references/specs/release-personas.md` § Stage 6
- `.claude/rules/release-process.md` § Stage 6
- `.claude/hooks/block-destructive.sh` (optional defense-in-depth — BLOCK-DESTRUCTIVE-024 candidate)
- `release/governance/release-process.md` (canonical; mirrored to `.claude/rules/release-process.md`)
- `core/rules/git-workflow.md` (canonical; mirrored to `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`)

### Documentation Impact

- `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md` — update (link / update / brief reason: Procedure 3 Worktree Discipline gains explicit `--force-with-lease` anti-pattern + Wave-N parallel-Engineering safety discipline)
- `release/references/specs/release-personas.md` — update (Stage 6 anti-pattern list gains the force-push variant)
- `.claude/rules/release-process.md` — update (Stage 6 protocol gains Wave-N safety discipline; mirror pair updated)
- `.claude/hooks/block-destructive.sh` — optional update (BLOCK-DESTRUCTIVE-024 candidate)

### Dependencies

- Composes with the v18.01 Wave-N parallel-Engineering pattern (this release's empirical-grounding source)
- Composes with `core/rules/git-workflow.md` § What NOT To Do (the existing `--force` rule; this extends with `--force-with-lease` variant)

### Acceptance Criteria

21.title: [Research]: Agent orchestration mechanisms — SWOT, contract dimensions, and platform-fit analysis
21.body:
**filed: 2026-05-25**

### What is the gap / improvement?

The pmo-platform's current agent orchestration is centralized hub-spoke (per [`hub-spoke-bridge.md`](pmo-platform/reference/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md)). Every chip prompt, gate handoff, and Tier-2 escalation references "the Hub". Alternative orchestration mechanisms (decentralized, federated, hierarchical, sequential, group-chat, etc.) exist in multi-agent literature with different trade-offs across state management, conflict resolution, observability, and human-in-the-loop integration. The platform has no grounded comparison artifact for choosing between them.

This is the RESEARCH HALF of a two-part enhancement. The selection-layer / config-integration is deliberately deferred to Part 2 — it composes with #28 (unified global config) and #41 (per-space methodology split) at Part 2 time.

### Why is this needed?

- Hub-spoke is load-bearing — every chip prompt, gate handoff, and Tier-2 escalation references the Hub. Alternative mechanisms need a defined contract before any consumer can branch on them.
- The platform separates Process / Framework / Methodology / Tool layers ([`release-process.md`](.claude/rules/release-process.md) § Execution Framework Reference). Orchestration is the missing axis between Framework and Tool — but adding it without grounded research risks reinventing well-known multi-agent patterns.
- The operational space (Cowork file-driven) and the release space (Engineering chip-driven) may have genuinely different orchestration needs. #41 establishes the per-space precedent for methodology; the same axis applies to orchestration.
- Without this research, Part 2's per-mechanism implementation specs would be designed against an undefined contract — exactly the kind of premise problem Tier 0 re-review catches.
- pmo-platform is broadening from PMO governance toward coding / portfolio / program management. Different problem classes (sequential pipelines, parallel-with-task-pool, divergent-then-merge, hierarchical decomposition) need different orchestration. Without a grounded taxonomy + per-class mechanism mapping, the platform risks shoehorning every workload into hub-spoke.

### Proposed change

Author one research artifact at `pmo-platform/reference/explanation/orchestration-mechanisms.md` (K1 codified-knowledge tier per [`knowledge-architecture.md`](pmo-platform/reference/explanation/knowledge-architecture.md)).

**Structure:**

- **§1. Background** — Process / Framework / Methodology / Tool layering; current hub-spoke as one realization of centralized orchestration.
- **§2. Contract dimensions** — the abstract interface ANY mechanism must satisfy:
  1. State management (where does pipeline state live?)
  2. Handoff protocol (how does work transfer between agents?)
  3. Conflict resolution (what if two agents claim the same artifact?)
  4. Observability (what events must be emitted? to what log surface?)
  5. Gate integration (how does [`gate-evaluation-spec.md`](pmo-platform/reference/schemas/gate-evaluation-spec.md) integrate?)
  6. Escalation paths (how does Tier 0/1/2/3 routing work?)
  7. Audit trail (what's the canonical change record?)
  8. Human-in-the-loop integration (where do operator gates land?)
  9. Problem-class fit (which task topologies does this mechanism serve well: sequential, parallel-with-pool, divergent-merge, hierarchical decomposition, conversational, market/auction)
- **§3. Mechanism-by-mechanism SWOT** — per-mechanism Strengths / Weaknesses / Opportunities / Threats, mapped against each §2 contract dimension. External citations (web-first per scoping decision; ≥3 per mechanism, academic OR industry-standard).
- **§3.5. Problem-class taxonomy** — enumerate the canonical task topologies pmo-platform may encounter across its expanded use cases (PMO governance, coding projects, portfolio/program management). For each:
  - Definition + canonical literature example
  - Indicator signals (how the platform recognizes the class)
  - Which §3 mechanisms serve it well, which poorly
  - Worked example from pmo-platform's current or anticipated workload (e.g., release-bundle = sequential-with-gates; coding-feature-review = hierarchical decomposition; backlog-grooming = work-stealing pool)
- **§4. Starting list** — which mechanisms the platform should support FIRST, with inclusion criteria justifying the selection. Candidate criteria menu the research evaluates:
  - (a) appears in ≥N peer-reviewed multi-agent papers
  - (b) has a working production realization in a comparable platform
  - (c) materially distinct from centralized hub-spoke on ≥3 contract dimensions
  - (d) operator-anticipated use case in pmo-platform / Cowork operational space
  - (e) materially improves fit for at least one problem class identified in §3.5 that hub-spoke does not well-serve
- **§5. Extension protocol** — how to add a new mechanism later: governance flow, contract conformance check, consumer-integration template.
- **§5.5. Selection trigger, evaluation timing, and selection discipline rules**

  **Trigger / timing (descriptive):**
  - Decision points: workspace init, project init, release planning (Stage 4), per-issue engineering (Stage 6), runtime per-task
  - Inputs to selection: problem class, scope size, parallelism opportunity, risk profile, human-gate density, reversibility tier
  - Re-evaluation triggers: under what conditions does an active workflow re-evaluate its orchestration mid-flight?

  **Selection discipline rules (governance constraints):**
  - DEFAULT: exactly ONE mechanism active per scope (task / workflow / release / project).
  - CASCADE: a parent workflow's mechanism choice applies to ALL child workflows within its scope. No per-child override; no nesting of different mechanisms.
  - EXCEPTION: composition (multiple mechanisms in one scope) requires explicit operator authorization. Agent MUST NOT combine mechanisms on its own. If operator requests composition without a documented plan, agent MUST surface a risk warning before proceeding.

  This section identifies TIMING, INPUTS, and DISCIPLINE RULES; it does NOT design the selection layer itself (per §7 deferral to Part 2 / #28).
- **§6. Composition with existing platform infrastructure:**
  - #28 unified global config (`orchestration_pattern` as one config field)
  - #41 per-space split (operational vs release orchestration)
  - [`decision-discipline.md`](pmo-platform/reference/standards/decision-discipline.md) DC1–DC4 universality axis
  - [`methodology-parameterization-v1.md`](pmo-platform/reference/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md) parameterization precedent
  - [`hub-spoke-bridge.md`](pmo-platform/reference/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md) as the centralized-mechanism reference implementation
- **§7. Out of scope (explicit deferrals)** — defends scope discipline:
  - Selection-layer design (defers to #28 / Part 2)
  - Consumer-skill changes (Part 2)
  - PROJECT.md / CLAUDE.md field additions (Part 2)
  - Implementation of any non-centralized mechanism (Part 2)
  - Auto-detection of problem class (Part 2; research only enumerates classes and maps mechanisms to them)
  - Runtime re-evaluation implementation (Part 2)
  - Composition / multi-mechanism orchestration is INTENTIONALLY NOT a supported default pattern. Implementation deferred indefinitely; activates only under operator-authorized exception per §5.5.

### Affected Files

- **NEW:** `pmo-platform/reference/explanation/orchestration-mechanisms.md` (research artifact)
- `pmo-platform/governance/roadmaps/automation.md` (cross-link new artifact in capability-vision tracking)

Stage 4/5 may identify additional cross-link consumers (e.g., [`architecture-overview.md`](pmo-platform/reference/explanation/architecture-overview.md) for layer-axis additions).

### Dependencies

- **Composes-with #28** (unified global config) — Part 2 of this enhancement reads the research output and contributes `orchestration_pattern` as a config field. No in-bundle blocker — research can fire any time.
- **Composes-with #41** (per-space methodology split) — the same per-space pattern (`operational_*` vs `release_*`) applies to orchestration. Part 2 inherits the per-space split for free.
- **Composes-with #104** (localized-context guardrail) — research artifact must conform to DC1–DC4 universality discipline (validated by `deploy.sh --check` Check 25).
- **Composes-with #32** (single canonical edit surface for spoke config) — Part 2's selection layer reuses the same single-surface consolidation pattern.

22.title: [Improvement]: Unified pmo-platform global config mechanism — plug-and-play methodology + parameterized choices consolidation
22.body:
**filed: 2026-05-25**

> _Four-digit `#1xxx`/`#2xxx` issue numbers and `v11.x`/`v12.x` labels below are historical citations in the pre-2026-06 re-versioning scheme (retained as record). Current-scheme cross-references and file paths have been reconciled to live homes; the quota-budget consumer relationship now points to its current-scheme issues (#23 / #24)._

### What is the gap / improvement?

The PMO platform has accumulated many "one-off global config items" scattered across governance, reference specs, and skill SKILL.md files. These are operator-customizable choices that should compose as a unified config surface — supporting plug-and-play methodology selection and other parameterized platform behavior. Today they live as:

- **`methodology-parameterization-v1.md` `delivery_approach`** field (Scrum / Kanban / XP / Waterfall / PRINCE2 / SAFe / Hybrid / Custom) — first-class parameterization, already in use
- **CLAUDE.md universal preferences** — decision discipline, reversibility tiers, evidence-quality labels (not currently parameterized; baked into universal rules)
- **Per-skill SKILL.md frontmatter** — `description:` / `model:` / `tools:` (Anthropic-frontmatter parameterized) + per-skill body conventions (PMO extensions, not parameterized)
- **Scattered thresholds** — release size targets (`5-8 issues per release`, `15-25 pts` from #1672), calibration intervals (`[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]`), staleness windows (`90-day re-verification` for upstream catalog), shakedown durations (`≥3 days warn-mode before flip-to-enforce`), oversize predicates (`size:XL` from #984), etc.
- **Recently introduced enum-class choices** (v11.27 surfacing as the trigger) — Release Class enum (#1669), 13-dim Readiness Scan dimensions (#1670), Bundle Composition Doctrine Frame (#1672 D-BundleDoctrineFrame), Discovery Discipline activation model (#1064)
- **Skill-specific config** — pmo-skill-editor `.editor-session` sentinel, hub-session-continuity surface paths, various `.claude/<allowlist>.txt` files

The trigger case is **D-BundleDoctrineFrame from #1672** (v11.27): the spoke surfaced 3 candidate real-world frames (F1 SAFe Feature-Slicing + Vertical Slice / F2 Continuous Delivery batching / F3 Lean Startup MVP — F3 not recommended). Operator stated: *"pmo-platform should be able to accommodate any of the methodologies/techniques with a default set in config possibly? This works with the plug and play concept."*

For v11.27 we default to F1 (agile/SAFe) without a config mechanism — Engineering ships F1 with frame-pluggability discipline (doctrine authored as "current default per platform config" with pluggable-frame language). This Enhancement implements the actual config mechanism that supports operator config-set on creation + config-update during platform operation.

### Why is this needed?

**Without unified config:**
- Operator-customizable choices are scattered across ≥10 files; no single source of truth
- Adding a new methodology/technique (e.g., XP-flavored bundling) requires hand-editing multiple files
- Defaults are buried in prose ("recommended 5-8 issues per release") rather than queryable
- `release-planner` / hub / spokes can't read a single config to parameterize behavior
- Future operators (or future agents) can't discover what's configurable without reading every governance file
- The plug-and-play promise (per platform vision memory: PgM/PM/Portfolio humans + agents-for-everything-else) requires the human/agent surface to be queryable, not prose-scattered

**With unified config:**
- Single file (or single index pointing to per-domain configs) lists ALL operator-parameterized choices with current values + defaults + allowed-values
- `release-planner` invokes the config at Mode A; spokes read it during Solutioning
- New methodology adoption = edit one config field, not rewrite multiple specs
- Calibration loops + `[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` thresholds become explicit config fields with calibration history
- Audit trail of config changes via git history

### Proposed change

Design + ship a **unified platform-config mechanism** with three deliverables:

1. **Canonical config surface** — new file at `release/governance/platform-config.yaml` (D-Format: YAML structured) OR `release/references/specs/platform-config.md` (D-Format: markdown with structured fields). Stage 5 settles. Format must support:
   - Operator-set defaults per category (methodology / sizing / thresholds / cadence / etc.)
   - Allowed-values enum per field (where applicable; e.g., `bundle_doctrine_frame: F1-safe-vertical-slice` from {F1, F2, F3, HYBRID})
   - Calibration history per field (where `[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` applies)
   - Cutover SHA per field-change (per existing cutover discipline)

2. **Consumer integration** — release-planner skill Mode A reads the config at session start; per-stage spokes read relevant fields; hub Procedure 0 references the config for spoke-prompt parameterization. Stage 5 designs the exact consumer protocol (where each consumer reads from + what happens when config field absent + default fallback).

3. **Config-update protocol** — config changes follow CLAUDE.md "No ungoverned changes" rule: GitHub Issue + plan + PR. Specific protocol design for config-change-only PRs (lighter weight than full release? or normal release flow?) — Stage 5 surfaces D-decision.

### Composition with v11.27 and other in-flight work

- **#1672 (Bundle Composition Doctrine, IN v11.27)** — D-BundleDoctrineFrame becomes a config field once this Enhancement ships. v11.27 ships F1 as hardcoded default with frame-pluggability discipline; this Enhancement promotes it to config-driven.
- **#1669 (Release Class taxonomy, IN v11.27)** — Class enum (4-value: routine / novel / cross-cutting / hotfix) becomes operator-customizable per platform config.
- **#1670 (13-dim Readiness Scan, IN v11.27)** — dim count + per-dim mechanism could become config fields.
- **#984 (Decomposition-review enforcement, IN v11.27)** — oversize predicates (currently hardcoded `size:XL` + AC ≥ 7 + file ≥ 5) become tunable config fields per operator preference.
- **#1064 (Discovery Discipline, IN v11.27)** — D-DiscoveryActivationModel (currently Universal-preference clause only) could become config-driven (always-active vs trigger-based).
- **Quota-budget work #23 / #24 (v12.13.1 candidates)** — the quota-budget pre-check uses operator-stated quota state today (no platform query); future config could hold operator's typical 5-hour-window envelope as a default + per-batch override surface.
- **`methodology-parameterization-v1.md` `delivery_approach`** — composes cleanly; existing parameterization extends into the new unified surface, OR `methodology-parameterization-v1.md` stays the canonical home for delivery_approach and the new config indexes it.

### Affected files (Stage 5 sharpens; Stage 4 directional)

- NEW `release/governance/platform-config.yaml` OR `release/references/specs/platform-config.md` (Stage 5 decides format + location)
- `release/references/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md` — compose with delivery_approach
- `release/skills/release-planner/SKILL.md` — Mode A reads config
- `release/skills/release-executor/SKILL.md` — Mode A reads config
- `.claude/agents/pmo-*.md` (7 agent definitions) — spokes reference config per stage
- `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md` — Procedure 0 parameterizes spoke prompts via config
- `CLAUDE.md` — Universal Preferences section may move per-platform-customizable items into config
- `core/governance/OPERATIONS.md` — cross-project rules section composes with config
- `release/references/standards/bundle-composition-doctrine.md` (post-v11.27) — reads `bundle_doctrine_frame` field; doctrine prose stays frame-pluggable
- Many other reference docs need cross-reference edits to point at config

### Dependencies

- **Composes-with #1672 (IN v11.27)** — v11.27 ships F1 hardcoded; this Enhancement promotes to config-driven (no cross-milestone blocking)
- **Composes-with quota-budget work #23 / #24 (v12.13.1)** — quota-state config field is a future consumer
- **Composes-with `methodology-parameterization-v1.md`** existing infrastructure
- **No in-bundle blockers** — Enhancement can fire any time post-v11.27

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Canonical config surface authored at agreed location/format (D-decision at Stage 5)
- [ ] Config schema supports: operator-set defaults, allowed-values enum, calibration history, cutover SHA per field-change
- [ ] release-planner skill Mode A reads config at session start
- [ ] At least 3 consumer-integration examples wired (e.g., bundle_doctrine_frame for #1672, release_class_enum for #1669, oversize_predicates for #984)
- [ ] Config-update protocol documented (governance flow for config-change-only PRs)
- [ ] `methodology-parameterization-v1.md` composes cleanly with new config (no duplication; clear ownership)
- [ ] Cutover clause anchored to this release's merge SHA with explicit `this release itself is exempt`
- [ ] Stage 13 release notes flag user-facing API change (new config surface is operator-discoverable)
- [ ] Audit trail: git history of config field changes is the canonical change record

### Evidence (per CLAUDE.md evidence-quality labels)

- **[SOURCE]** Operator-stated at v11.27 Collective Review 2026-05-25: *"pmo-platform should be able to accommodate any of the methodologies/techniques with a default set in config possibly? This works with the plug and play concept. You can probably create the comment or enhancement for the config ( there are a lot of one off global config items now across the pmo-platform release and operations). For now we can default to the agile version. Enhancement would need to set this config on creation and update."*
- **[CONTEXT]** Trigger case: v11.27 #1672 D-BundleDoctrineFrame surfaced 3 candidate frames + need for parameterization
- **[CONTEXT]** Existing partial-parameterization: `methodology-parameterization-v1.md` `delivery_approach` field
- **[INFERRED]** Inventory of scattered global config items in the proposed-change § above is illustrative, not exhaustive; Stage 5 produces the full survey via R1 Evidence-Grounding
- **[RECOMMENDED]** Target milestone: TBD (operator triage); not v11.27 (scope hard-locked) and not v12.13.1 (different scope class). Priority P2-P3 (operationally enabling for future methodology adoption + reduces governance maintenance burden but not blocking).

### Composition with quota-budget work #23 / #24 (v12.13.1)

Quota-state input for the dual-checkpoint quota-budget gate (#23) is a future consumer of this config — operator's typical 5-hour-window envelope held as a default; per-batch operator override stays the runtime-checkpoint mechanism. This Enhancement provides the surface where the default lives.

### Composition with `pmo-platform vision`

Per memory `project_platform_vision.md` (self-improving loop) + `project_product_vision.md` (PgM/PM/Portfolio humans served by agent ecosystem at principal level): the plug-and-play config mechanism is the surface humans and agents both use to set platform behavior. Without it, methodology adoption (e.g., onboarding a Kanban team vs SAFe org) requires expert-level platform editing rather than config-set operation.



---

## Scope clarification — relationship-mapping config (2026-06-06)

Operator direction 2026-06-06: name relationship portability as one of the parameterized choices this unified config consolidates, tying it to the plug-and-play goal this ticket already invokes.

Add to the config's parameterized-choice surface:

- **Source ticketing system selection** — which external system(s) are active for a given install / project.
- **Per-system relationship-maintenance posture** — read-only / one-way push / two-way round-trip.
- **Canonical→native relationship-type mapping overrides** — per-system deviations from the default mapping.

This is the config surface that drives the adapter relationship contract (#11) over the canonical relationship model (#409). It is the relationship slice of the plug-and-play promise (#14) this ticket already names — "accommodate any of the methodologies/techniques with a default set in config … works with the plug and play concept."

23.title: [Improvement]: Dual-checkpoint quota-budget gate — Stage 4 plan-time estimate + Procedure 2 runtime re-validation (v12.13.1 candidate; sibling to #2686)
23.body:
**filed: 2026-05-25**

> _The sibling quota-constraint issue (the "5-hour usage limit documentation") is #24 in the current scheme; references below are reconciled accordingly. Four-digit `#1xxx`/`#2xxx` numbers and `v11.x`/`v12.x` labels are historical citations from the pre-2026-06 re-versioning scheme (retained as record); file paths are reconciled to current homes._

### What is the gap / improvement?

Sibling to [#24](https://github.com/cody-hutson/pmo-platform/issues/24) (per-account session-quota constraint — 5-hour usage limit documentation + runtime mitigation patterns).

**#24 documents** the constraint and proposes runtime mitigations (quota budgeting, window-aware timing, serialize-on-failure, reduce per-spoke consumption).

**This issue implements** the active enforcement mechanism: a **dual-checkpoint quota-budget gate** that fires (a) at Stage 4 plan-time and (b) **on every Procedure 2 routing decision before launching parallel subagents**. The runtime checkpoint is the load-bearing piece — Stage 4 estimates the budget once, but mid-release quota drift (operator does other work between routings; 5-hour boundary crosses; per-spoke costs vary from baseline) means a one-and-done check at Stage 4 misses cases the runtime check would catch.

### Why is this needed?

The v11.27 hub session (first post-v12.13 release) hit the 5-hour usage limit when launching 9 parallel Stage 5 spokes — all 9 returned `"session limit · resets 8:50pm"` with cumulative ~7,800 tokens (pure startup; no work completed). The failure surfaced at execution time when the cause was visible at planning/routing time (operator had drawn down 5-hour-window quota before the batch fired).

Without an active gate:
- Stage 4 planning doesn't know parallel-eligible spoke count vs quota envelope
- Procedure 2 routing launches N parallel subagents without checking whether the launch will fit in remaining quota
- Failure surfaces at execution time, wasting (a) per-spoke startup tokens that don't accomplish work, (b) hub-side time recovering and re-launching, (c) operator attention triaging
- The pattern recurs on every release with N ≥ 4-5 parallel-eligible spokes when operator quota is non-fresh

The runtime check matters more than the plan-time check: Stage 4 plans the budget once based on initial state, but parallel batches fire at multiple routing points across a release (Stage 5 batch / Stage 7 batch / Stage 8 batch / etc.). Each batch faces a potentially different remaining-quota envelope. The ongoing check catches mid-release drift; plan-time alone doesn't.

### Proposed change — dual-checkpoint design

#### Checkpoint A — Stage 4 plan-time budget estimate

New phase in `release/references/pipeline/stage-04-planning.md` — likely `A9: Quota-Budget Pre-Check` (alongside A1 Release Readiness, A4 Cross-PR Overlap, A8 Critical Path).

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Parallel-eligible spoke count per stage type | Stage 4 applicability matrix (Stages 5/7/8 are parallel-safe per Procedure 2) |
| Estimated tokens per spoke | Historical median from `pipeline-event-log.md` (if telemetry extended per below) OR heuristic (size:S/M/L/XL bucket scaling) |
| Cumulative work estimate | spokes × per-spoke estimate, per parallel batch |
| Fresh-window quota envelope | Conservative default (e.g., known plan-tier ceiling) OR operator-stated at hub start |
| Estimated quota draw at execution time | Cumulative estimate ÷ envelope as % per batch |

**Output routing tree (mirrors #984's decomposition-review pattern):**

```
PASS  (cumulative << envelope)     → proceed parallel; no warning in plan
WARN  (cumulative ≈ envelope)      → recommend stagger (rate-limit defense) + window-aware timing in plan
FAIL  (cumulative > envelope)      → 3 outcomes:
                                      (a) split-batch (run in multiple windows)
                                      (b) reduce per-spoke cost (compact prompts, narrower scope)
                                      (c) escalate Tier 2 [SCOPE CHANGE] (reduce release size)
```

Output lands in the Stage 4 release plan as `### Quota Budget` section alongside Risk Register / A8 Critical Path / A4 Cross-PR Overlap.

#### Checkpoint B — Procedure 2 routing-time re-validation (load-bearing)

**This is the ongoing check, fires before EVERY parallel-subagent launch — not just once at Stage 4.**

New step in `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md § Procedure 2` (and a symmetric add to `Procedure 3 § Spoke Launch Mechanisms` since that's where the actual `Agent({...})` invocation happens):

Before issuing N parallel Agent calls in the same hub message, hub runs:

```
1. Compute N_planned (parallel-eligible sub-tasks at this routing point per Procedure 2)
2. Estimate cumulative cost: N_planned × per-spoke-cost-estimate (from Stage 4 budget OR refined from prior spokes' actuals in pipeline-event-log)
3. Compare against remaining-window envelope:
   - Default: operator-stated quota state at hub session start (`fresh` / `partial-N%` / `near-tail`)
   - Future: queryable from platform if API exposes it
   - Elapsed-window time since hub start contributes to refinement
4. Render verdict:
   - PROCEED  → launch all N in parallel (existing behavior)
   - STAGGER  → launch with in-prompt sleep stagger (rate-limit defense; partial-quota-window mitigation)
   - SERIALIZE → launch one at a time, halt on first failure
   - DEFER    → hold batch for next 5-hour window; surface to operator with reset-time estimate
5. If WARN/FAIL: produce Decision Briefing surfacing the verdict + recommendation to operator BEFORE launching
```

The runtime check uses Stage 4's plan as the baseline budget but adjusts for: (a) actual per-spoke costs observed in earlier spokes this release, (b) elapsed-window time, (c) operator-stated quota updates (e.g., "I just did other work" / "fresh quota").

**Key design question (defer to Stage 5):** How does the hub know operator's current quota state? Options:
- (a) AskUserQuestion at hub session start capturing initial state (`fresh` / `partial` / `near-tail`); propagates to every routing decision with elapsed-time adjustment
- (b) Per-batch AskUserQuestion before launching parallel spokes (more friction; more accurate)
- (c) Future: platform-side quota API (currently not queryable from within a session)
- (d) Hybrid: session-start capture + per-batch optional override

Stage 5 spec settles the operator-interaction surface.

### Composition

- **#24** (sibling) — #24 documents the constraint + proposes runtime mitigations; THIS issue implements the active enforcement gate that operationalizes those mitigations
- **#984 (Decomposition-review enforcement on oversized work items — IN v11.27)** — structural parallel. Both produce the same routing tree shape (kept / split / escalate); both pre-execution gates against capacity issues. The quota-budget pre-check is essentially "decomposition review for parallel launch batches" — same family, different surface (work-item size vs parallel-batch size).
- **#983/#979 (audit-trail + release-synthesis — shipped v12.13)** — pipeline-event-log infrastructure is the natural place for spoke token-consumption telemetry that the budget estimate consumes. Proposal: extend the event schema to capture `tokens_used` per `spoke-completion` event. Backwards-compatible (new optional field).
- **`[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` framework** — quota-estimate thresholds (parallel-batch-size warn/fail trigger; per-spoke cost baseline) get same calibration treatment as other v11.20+ thresholds. Re-tunes after 3 post-cutover releases.
- **`hub-action-tracking.md`** — runtime check could emit action-item entries to `release/releases/hub-state/vX.Y/action-items.md` when DEFER fires (e.g., "Resume Stage 5 batch after window-reset at HH:MM").

### Affected files

- `release/references/pipeline/stage-04-planning.md` — Checkpoint A (Stage 4 plan-time)
- `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md` — Checkpoint B (Procedure 2 + Procedure 3 routing-time)
- `.claude/rules/release-process.md` + `release/governance/release-process.md` (canonical) — § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules table extends with quota-gate column
- `release/references/standards/pipeline-event-log-schema.md` — extend `spoke-completion` event with optional `tokens_used` field
- `release/references/specs/release-personas.md` — Stage 4 persona behavioral marker for quota-budget estimation; hub Procedure 2 ongoing-gate discipline
- New possible file: `release/references/standards/quota-budget-protocol.md` (canonical spec for the dual checkpoint) — Stage 5 decides new file vs section in stage-04-planning.md

### Dependencies

- **Composes with #24** (sibling; both v12.13.1 candidates)
- **Composes with #984** (work-item decomposition review — IN v11.27; same routing-tree shape; #984's Stage 5 design may inform the verdict-routing schema for THIS issue's Stage 5)
- **No in-bundle blockers** (#24 ships the constraint documentation; this issue implements the active gate)
- **Cutover discipline:** applies to releases entering Stage 4 strictly AFTER v12.13.1 merge SHA; **v12.13.1 itself exempt**.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `stage-04-planning.md` gains new phase (A9 or A4.5) Quota-Budget Pre-Check with input table + routing tree
- [ ] Stage 4 release plan output gains `### Quota Budget` section (alongside Risk Register etc.)
- [ ] `hub-spoke-bridge.md § Procedure 2` gains new step "Quota check before parallel launch" with PROCEED/STAGGER/SERIALIZE/DEFER routing
- [ ] `hub-spoke-bridge.md § Procedure 3 § Spoke Launch Mechanisms` gains corresponding pre-launch invocation hook
- [ ] `release-process.md § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules` table notes that "parallel-safe" is coordination semantics, not quota semantics; quota gate runs orthogonally
- [ ] `pipeline-event-log-schema.md` extends `spoke-completion` event with optional `tokens_used` field
- [ ] Mirror-pair sync (Check 9) enforced for any mirror-pair file edits
- [ ] Cutover clause `v12.13.1 itself is exempt` present anchored to v12.13.1 merge SHA
- [ ] Operator-interaction surface for quota-state capture resolved at Stage 5 D-Gate
- [ ] Calibration trigger registered at `RELEASE_LOG.md` `[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` baseline maintenance for parallel-batch-size + per-spoke-cost thresholds
- [ ] First-failure evidence (v11.27 Stage 5 launch 2026-05-24) preserved as canonical empirical reference

### Evidence (per CLAUDE.md evidence-quality labels)

- **[SOURCE]** v11.27 hub session 2026-05-24 ~20:00–20:50 [timezone]: 9-spoke parallel launch all hit 5-hour usage limit (Issue #24 documents the failure).
- **[SOURCE]** Operator clarification 2026-05-24 (post-#24 filing): "I want to clarify that this would need to be an ongoing task before writing subagents not a one and done" — established the runtime-check requirement.

v12.13 ships parallel-Agent-tool orchestration (per `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md § Spoke Launch Mechanisms`) with the canonical recommendation that Stage 5 spokes fire in parallel:

> "When Procedure 2 routing identifies multiple actionable sub-tasks in parallel (e.g., Stage 5 across several issues), the hub issues one Agent invocation per actionable sub-task in the same response"

And per `.claude/rules/release-process.md § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules`:

> "Stage 5 Solutioning | YES — parallel-safe | Spokes post sub-task comments only; no commit/file write on release branch or main | Output channel is GitHub Issue comment — no contention surface."

**Real-world drift discovered during v11.27 hub execution (2026-05-24, ~20:00–20:50 [timezone], post-v12.13 first live-fire release):** Launching 9 Stage 5 spokes in parallel via Agent tool exhausted the operator's 5-hour session quota near-instantly. All 9 spokes returned `"You've hit your session limit · resets 8:50pm ([timezone])"` with cumulative token usage of ~7,800 across all 9 spokes (no spoke completed any solutioning work; pure startup-overhead consumption). State recovery: 9 sub-tasks remain OPEN with zero comments + 1 orphan worktree (`agent-a0da35a22ba2dfb5b`).

The v12.13 design does not account for per-account session-quota concurrent-draw interaction. The spec assumes Agent-tool spawn is quota-free; in practice, each spawned session reserves quota share that — when 9 concurrent sessions reserve simultaneously — exceeds the operator's available quota envelope.

### Why is this needed?

Without this guidance, future post-v12.13 releases will hit the same failure mode on every release with ≥4-5 Stage 5 issues. v11.27 is the FIRST post-v12.13 release per the cross-account efficacy test (per memory `project_v12_13_automation_efficacy_test.md`); the test was scoped specifically to surface this class of drift.

Operationally: the failure mode wastes ~10 minutes per affected launch (spokes spawn, hit limit, return failed), plus operator time for re-launch coordination. At Stage 5 only this is recoverable; at later stages (Stage 6 Engineering with commits + PR open) it would be more expensive.

### Proposed change

1. **Update `hub-spoke-bridge.md § Spoke Launch Mechanisms`** to add a new subsection `### Per-Account Quota Constraint` documenting:
   - Per-account 5-hour Opus quota envelope (cite source: operator-stated 2026-05-24)
   - Concurrent-draw failure mode: N parallel Agent spawns × per-spawn reservation > quota
   - Mitigation patterns: staggered-start (in-prompt sleep) / batched waves / serial fallback
   - Empirical reference: v11.27 first-failure 2026-05-24 with N=9

2. **Update `.claude/rules/release-process.md § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules`** Stage 5 row to add a column or note: "subject to per-account session-quota envelope — see hub-spoke-bridge.md § Per-Account Quota Constraint for staggering/batching mitigation"

3. **Surface staggering mechanism canonically** — codify the in-prompt sleep pattern (where each parallel-launched spoke begins its task with `sleep <position * delay_seconds>` to stagger actual work) as a default for hub Procedure 2 Stage 5 / 7 / 8 parallel launches when N ≥ 4

4. **Calibration trigger** — recommend `[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` MEDIUM confidence on the staggering threshold (4 vs 5 vs 6 spoke count threshold; 30s vs 45s vs 60s delay) post v11.27, v12.13.1, and 1 additional release

### Affected files

- `release/references/how-to/hub-spoke-bridge.md` — § Spoke Launch Mechanisms (new subsection)
- `.claude/rules/release-process.md` + `release/governance/release-process.md` (canonical) — § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules Stage 5 row
- `release/references/specs/release-personas.md` — Stage 5 persona (possibly add anti-pattern: "does not assume parallel-safe means quota-free")

### Dependencies

- Composes with v11.27 #2641 (spoke return-value discipline) — that issue makes spoke output more compact, which could reduce per-spoke token consumption (smaller marginal quota impact). Composes informationally; no blocking sequence edge.
- Composes with the cross-account efficacy-test memory finding (per `project_v12_13_automation_efficacy_test.md`)
- Cutover discipline: applies to releases entering Stage 5 strictly AFTER v12.13.1 merge SHA; **v12.13.1 itself exempt**.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hub-spoke-bridge.md § Spoke Launch Mechanisms` gains `### Per-Account Quota Constraint` subsection with mitigation patterns
- [ ] `release-process.md § Procedure 2 § Parallelism Rules` Stage 5 row notes the quota-envelope subject
- [ ] Mirror-pair sync enforced via Check 9
- [ ] Cutover clause `v12.13.1 itself is exempt` present anchored to v12.13.1 merge SHA
- [ ] Calibration trigger registered at `release/releases/RELEASE_LOG.md` `[CALIBRATE-AFTER-3]` baseline maintenance
- [ ] First-failure evidence (v11.27 Stage 5 launch 2026-05-24, this issue) preserved as canonical empirical reference

### Evidence (per CLAUDE.md evidence-quality labels)

- **[SOURCE]** v11.27 hub session 2026-05-24 ~20:00–20:50 [timezone]: launched 9 Stage 5 spokes via Agent tool with `model: "opus"` + `isolation: "worktree"` + `run_in_background: true` per current spec. All 9 returned session-limit error with low token counts. Sub-tasks #2643–#2651 all remain OPEN with zero comments.
- **[SOURCE]** Operator-stated context 2026-05-24: "I was towards end of usage for 5hr" — confirms 5-hour Opus quota window AND that prior usage contributed to the failure
- **[CONTEXT]** Memory `project_v12_13_automation_efficacy_test.md` scoped this kind of finding: "The efficacy test will surface real-world drift between spec'd behavior and observed behavior — surface any such drift as Tier 2 [SCOPE CHANGE] candidates for a v12.13.1 patch release"
- **[INFERRED]** Per-account 5-hour Opus quota envelope; exact token-count limit and per-session reservation share are unknown — Stage 5 of this v12.13.1 issue surfaces this as a D-gate to be resolved.
- **[RECOMMENDED]** Target milestone: v12.13.1 (patch release). Priority P2 (operationally blocking for releases with N≥4 parallel-eligible Stage 5/7/8 issues — that's the majority of releases).

32.title: [Enhancement]: User-configurable methodology hybrid-two + per-space (operational vs release) methodology split
32.body:
**filed: 2026-05-24**

### Category
Enhancement

### Description

The `delivery_approach` enum in `project-schema.md` supports 8 archetypes (Scrum / Kanban / XP / Waterfall / PRINCE2 / SAFe / Hybrid / Custom) but has two structural limitations:

**Limitation 1:** "Hybrid" is rigidly defined as the SPM-co-managed pattern (one iterative track + one phase-gated track per R8 semantic anchor). Users wanting any other two-archetype combo (Scrum + Kanban = Scrumban; Waterfall + XP = predictive-front-loaded with TDD) must drop to "Custom" and populate the full `custom_methodology_definition` block — significant friction for what should be a 2-archetype selection.

**Limitation 2:** Single `delivery_approach` per PROJECT.md. Real projects often run different methodologies in different SPACES (Kanban-flow ops + Stage-Gate releases). Current schema can't represent this; users either drop to Custom or lose one methodology.

Together these block plug-and-play onboarding readiness.

### Evidence

- [SOURCE: `core/schemas/project-schema.md` line 43] — `delivery_approach: Scrum | Kanban | XP | Waterfall | PRINCE2 | SAFe | Hybrid | Custom` — single value
- [SOURCE: `release/references/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md` § Hybrid line 101] — "In v11.01, 'Hybrid' means the SPM-co-managed pattern... Single-track projects that run 'mostly-Scrum-with-light-gate-review' are NOT Hybrid — they classify as Scrum"
- [CONTEXT] — operator directive 2026-05-24: "methodologies are hybrid or single select. pmo-platform should support all with user config against a specific one or hybrid two... prevent confusion in both operational and release spaces"
- [INFERRED] — Custom escape requires authoring 8+ frontmatter fields; two-archetype hybrid should be a 1-line declaration

### Affected Files

- `core/schemas/project-schema.md` (edit — extend `delivery_approach` to accept single archetype OR 2-element array; add optional `operational_methodology` + `release_methodology` fields)
- `release/references/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md` (edit — relax Hybrid semantic anchor; add Hybrid-Two pattern; document per-space methodology pattern)
- `release/references/specs/methodology-archetype-matrix.md` (edit — add 2-archetype hybrid matrix rows)
- Skills consuming `delivery_approach` (audit per Stage 5 — `release-planner`, `delivery-engine`, and the engineering-stage skills, etc.)

### Proposed Change

Extend `delivery_approach` to accept either single archetype (current) OR a 2-element array of named archetypes (new Hybrid-Two pattern). Add optional `operational_methodology` + `release_methodology` fields for per-space methodology split. Update consumption pattern in `methodology-parameterization-v1.md § Skill Consumption Pattern` to handle 2-array + per-space variants. 43.body:
**filed: 2026-05-24**

### Priority

P3 - Medium

### Category

Structure

### Description

`deploy.sh` inlines four large bash arrays as constants: `SKILL_LIST` (21 entries), `HARNESS_LIST`, `HARNESS_OPERATOR_STATE`, and `TEMPLATE_SYNC_MAP` (31 entries). Adding a skill / harness artifact / template-sync mapping requires editing the script itself — friction for routine config changes. This sub-Issue moves each to a flat manifest file under `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/manifests/`; tooling reads the manifests at runtime.

This is **Sub-Issue D** of #57 (umbrella). Sequenced after Sub-Issue A (relocation); parallelizes with Sub-Issue B (check registry).

### Evidence

- [SOURCE: deploy.sh:10-32] — `SKILL_LIST` inline bash array, 21 entries
- [SOURCE: deploy.sh:53] — `HARNESS_LIST` inline bash array
- [SOURCE: deploy.sh:58-61] — `HARNESS_OPERATOR_STATE` inline bash array
- [SOURCE: deploy.sh:78-115] — `TEMPLATE_SYNC_MAP` inline bash array, 31 entries
- [INFERRED] — Issue history shows multiple "register X in SKILL_LIST" / "add to HARNESS_LIST" Issues (e.g., #244 eval-writer registration, #242 SKILL_LIST count reconciliation) — friction signal
- [SOURCE: #57 § Config-as-data axis] — parent umbrella identifies this gap as the config-as-data axis

### Affected Files

- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/manifests/skills.txt` (new — replaces `SKILL_LIST`)
- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/manifests/harness-artifacts.txt` (new — replaces `HARNESS_LIST`)

- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/manifests/template-sync-map.txt` (new — replaces `TEMPLATE_SYNC_MAP`)

- `pmo-platform/engineering/tools/checks/check-*.sh` (edit — checks reading these constants now source via the manifest reader)

### Proposed Change

After this Issue ships, adding a skill / harness artifact / template-sync mapping is a flat-file edit (one line per addition), NOT a script edit. Manifests are human-readable, line-oriented, supporting comments (`#`-prefixed lines) and skippable blank lines.

The manifest format is the simplest portable representation: one entry per line, semicolon-separated fields if multi-field (like `TEMPLATE_SYNC_MAP`). Tooling reads via a shared `read_manifest()` library function that strips comments and blanks.

Exact format and library shape deferred to Stage 5 Solutioning.

Parent: #57. Hard requires Sub-Issue A (relocation) merged first. Parallelizes with Sub-Issue B (check registry).

326.title: [Structure]: Orphan-state sweep must gate on process-liveness, not branch-name/merge heuristics
326.body:
### Priority

P3 - Medium

### Category

Structure

### Description

The orphan-state sweep decides worktree-removal eligibility from **branch-name pattern** (`claude/*`, `release/*`, `chore/*`), **merged-state**, **dirty-check**, and an **"active worktree attached"** test. None of these prove a worktree is *idle*. A merged, clean worktree can still be **actively held by a live session** — removing it deletes that session's working directory mid-run (the cwd-was-deleted failure).

The sweep must treat **"held by a live process" as a hard non-eligible state**, determined from process evidence, and that state must **override** the branch-name / merge / recency eligibility signals. Liveness is knowable, not a guess — it should not be inferred from how recently a tree was touched.

### Evidence

- [SOURCE: release/tools/cleanup-orphan-state.sh] `classify_worktree` keys on branch pattern + `worktree_is_clean` + `branch_has_worktree`; a scan for `ps`/`pgrep`/lock-file inspection in the script returns nothing — there is no process-liveness gate.
- [CONTEXT] git records a lock holder for an attached worktree under its worktree metadata; the live holder is independently observable in the OS process table. Liveness can be derived by intersecting the two.
- [INFERRED] A merged-clean `claude/*` worktree held by a concurrent live session is removal-eligible under today's heuristics — the self-/sibling-reap failure mode.

### Affected Files

release/tools/cleanup-orphan-state.sh (edit — add a process-liveness pre-filter to worktree classification; extend `--self-test`)

### Documentation Impact

None — no K1 codified-documentation change required (rationale: behavioral gate inside an engineering tool; a Stage 5 spec note is optional, not a declared K1 target). [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] Stage 5 may elect to add a one-line note to the cleanup-tools spec.

### Proposed Change

The sweep never removes a worktree that a live process holds. Liveness is a hard SKIP that takes precedence over branch-name, merged-state, and recency. The report distinguishes "skipped — live session" from "skipped — dirty" and "skipped — attached." Mechanism for *computing* liveness (lock-holder ↔ process-table intersection, portability) is deferred to Stage 5. [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] mechanism TBD at Stage 5.

### Dependencies

_None known at intake._

### Risks & Cross-Cutting Impact

- [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] The liveness oracle must be portable (macOS is the current host); an oracle that *under-detects* live holders re-introduces the reap risk it is meant to remove.
- None otherwise identified.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A worktree held by a live session is classified non-removable (SKIP) in both `--dry-run` and `--apply`, regardless of merged/clean state (method: `--self-test` fixture with a synthetic live holder).
- [ ] A removal pass leaves every live-held worktree intact (method: enumerate live holders before/after an `--apply`; the set is unchanged).
- [ ] The report labels a liveness-skip distinctly from a dirty-skip and an attached-skip (method: grep report output for the three distinct reasons).
- [ ] `--self-test` exercises the live-holder SKIP path and exits 0 (method: run `--self-test`).

### Notes

Generalizes a prior self-cwd-protection concern from the repo's earlier issue lineage (which protected only the tree the sweep itself runs from) to **all** concurrent live sessions. Likely home: the cleanup-tools milestone. Surfaced by a 2026-06-03 memory audit of the worktree-cleanup discipline.

327.title: [Structure]: Public-flip commit-message scan omits personal-email patterns
327.body:
### Priority

P2 - High

### Category

Structure

### Description

The public-flip leak scan inspects **new commit messages** in a PR range for version-lineage tokens, issue/PR numbers, and GitHub handle URLs — but **not personal-email patterns**. A personal email committed into a message or a co-author trailer is **permanent on merge** (it lives in history and cannot be removed without a history rewrite), and the pre-commit PII guard scans the **staged diff**, not the message. The union of the two controls leaves one surface uncovered: a personal email in a commit message or trailer reaches history unguarded at both pre-commit and PR time.

### Evidence

- [SOURCE: .github/workflows/public-flip-scan.yml] the new-commit-message step's pattern matches version-lineage tokens, `#N`, and github.com handle URLs; there is no email alternation in that pattern.
- [SOURCE: core/hooks/git-pre-commit-pii.sh] scans `git diff --cached` added lines with a personal-email alternation — but does not inspect the commit message or trailer.
- [INFERRED] The union of these two controls leaves "personal email in a commit message / co-author trailer" uncovered.

### Affected Files

.github/workflows/public-flip-scan.yml (edit — extend the new-commit-message scan) and/or scan.sh (edit — add the personal-email class to the message surface). [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] exact locus identified at Stage 5.

### Documentation Impact

None — no K1 codified-documentation change required (rationale: extends an existing CI scan's pattern coverage on a non-K1 surface; no user-facing doc target).

### Proposed Change

New commit messages in a PR range are scanned for personal-email patterns under the same monotonic-decrease (ratchet) posture as the existing leak classes, and the trailer line is in scope (not only subject/body). A re-introduced personal email in a message or trailer fails the gate **before** merge. Whether this reuses the pre-commit guard's email class or extends `scan.sh` is deferred to Stage 5; the constraint is a single source of truth for the pattern.

### Dependencies

_None known at intake._

### Risks & Cross-Cutting Impact

- [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] The accepted-home files (LICENSE / SECURITY / CODEOWNERS / FUNDING / ADRs) legitimately carry operator contact email, but those exemptions are *file*-scoped; commit messages are not files, so the home-exemption may not map cleanly — confirm the false-positive posture at Stage 5.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A PR whose new commit message or trailer contains a personal-email pattern fails the public-flip scan (method: fixture commit with a test address; gate exits non-zero).
- [ ] A PR with no personal email in its new messages passes (method: clean fixture; exit 0).
- [ ] The check covers the co-author trailer line, not only the subject/body (method: trailer-only fixture).
- [ ] The personal-email pattern has a single source shared with the pre-commit guard (method: assert both reference the same class). [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] single-source mechanism set at Stage 5.

### Notes

Composes with — does not replace — the existing leak ratchet and the depersonalization gate. Surfaced by a 2026-06-03 memory audit of the leak-prevention tooling family.

351.title: [Structure]: Add a first-class domain / deliverable-type axis to PROJECT.md alongside delivery_approach
351.body:
**filed: 2026-05-16**

## Priority
P2 - High

## Category
Structure

## Description
The platform parameterizes *how work is governed* (`delivery_approach`: 8 methodology archetypes) but has no parameter for *what kind of work is being delivered*. A software fix, a website feature, a [ERP] customization, and a code-review task are indistinguishable to PROJECT.md and to every consumer skill. This single absence is the root cause that forces five downstream couplings (deploy model, verification surface, knowledge sourcing, backlog surface, non-deliverable lifecycle) to each fail independently per-domain. The platform is methodology-aware but domain-blind.

## Evidence
- [INFERRED, from the versatility-eval scoring matrix — analysis pack predates the 2026-06 re-versioning and is no longer in-tree] — 22 of 52 evaluated stage×domain cells are PG/DK/SI; every non-software domain degrades; H3 (pack pattern reaches only 2 of 22 skills) CONFIRMED.
- [SOURCE: release/references/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md §5] — the 3-branch skill-consumption pattern keys exclusively off `delivery_approach`; no domain branch exists.
- [SOURCE: core/schemas/project-schema.md] — frontmatter has `delivery_approach`, `custom_methodology_definition`, `spm_comanaged`; no `domain`/`deliverable_type` field.
- [INFERRED] R1–R5 in the same roadmap are individually necessary only because there is no domain axis to switch on; a domain axis is the keystone that makes them coherent rather than ad hoc.

## Affected Files
- core/schemas/project-schema.md (edit — add the new axis to the schema)
- release/references/specs/methodology-parameterization-v1.md (edit — sibling consumption pattern for the new axis)
- core/schemas/gate-criteria-spec.md (edit — gate criteria that vary by domain)
- [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] consumer skills that read PROJECT.md — full set identified in Planning

## Proposed Change
PROJECT.md can declare the work domain / deliverable type as a first-class, validated field, orthogonal to `delivery_approach`. Consumer skills and gate criteria can branch on it the way they already branch on methodology. The taxonomy of domains, the enum-vs-pack boundary, and the consumption contract are design decisions deferred to Stage 5 Solutioning ([ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] mechanism TBD at Stage 5 — likely mirrors the existing dimension/domain-pack pattern that already works for build-reviewer/implementation-planner).

## Dependencies
None (this is the keystone; R1–R5 depend on it, not the reverse).

## Risks & Cross-Cutting Impact
- [INFERRED, versatility-eval scoring] Touches the schema + every PROJECT.md consumer — high blast radius; sequence first so R1–R5 build on a stable axis.
- [ASSUMPTION – CONFIRM] May interact with `spm_comanaged` reconciliation; verify orthogonality at Solutioning.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verify that `project-schema.md` defines a domain/deliverable-type field with allowed values and validation rules (method: grep the schema for the new field + a V-rule).
- [ ] Verify that `methodology-parameterization-v1.md` contains a domain-axis consumption pattern parallel to its §5 methodology pattern (method: section present, references the new field).
- [ ] Confirm at least one gate criterion in `gate-criteria-spec.md` is conditioned on the domain axis (method: grep for the field name in a criterion row).
- [ ] Verify the change is additive — existing methodology-only PROJECT.md files still validate (method: regression check against an existing PROJECT.md).

## Notes
Keystone for roadmap R1–R5 (4-domain versatility evaluation). Reversibility: EXPENSIVE (schema + consumers), confidence MEDIUM — sequence and blast-radius resolved at Planning/Solutioning.
